source.title: Better & Faster Large Language Models via Multi-token Prediction
source.authors: Fabian Gloeckle; Badr Youbi Idrissi; Baptiste Rozière; D. Lopez-Paz; Gabriel Synnaeve

page_placements.theme: Training-induced look-ahead: objectives or data that target future tokens

record.tranche_reason: The study develops and evaluates a training method that explicitly predicts multiple future tokens. It does not test whether ordinary next-token models internally represent distant future tokens or whether intervening on such representations changes intermediate text.
record.gate_note: The paper discusses precomputing features for later tokens and reports downstream results after training with an explicit multi-token prediction objective. Those results do not directly measure internal look-ahead or its causal effect on generated intermediate text; the training objective induces future-token prediction. No rhyme-planning test, hidden-state probe of future tokens, or intervention on a candidate future token is reported.
record.test_reason: The study trains models with an explicit multi-token objective and reports only that method's downstream performance. Future-token prediction is induced on purpose, not measured arising in next-token models. Planning-related content is speculation: 2-token loss 'incentivizes models to precompute features', plus a citation of Future Lens. No probe, rhyme test, intervention or look-ahead depth measure is reported for any version. I classed it discusses/T6 rather than the reader's uses_without_test/T4, since it does not use the planning finding as a tool; either label leaves it untested.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. Authors conclude multi-token prediction improves sample efficiency and generative performance, increasingly with model size and especially on code. They posit it reduces teacher-forcing/autoregressive mismatch and gives about 3x faster inference via self-speculative decoding. Gains on small algorithmic tasks are attributed to easier information transfer across positions.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains models with an explicit multi-token prediction loss using a shared trunk and separate future-token heads. It does not use the original rhyme-planning intervention or hidden-state readout method.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported induction advantage depends on model size and dataset: it fades at 100M nonembedding parameters and above, and largely disappears with a 9:1 books/children-stories data mix except for the two smallest models. The paper also states that the optimal future-token window depends on input data distribution.

fits_no_version.finding: After MTP training, induction accuracy improves for models of 30M nonembedding parameters and below. The advantage disappears at 100M and above, and with a books/children-stories mix except for the smallest models.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Multi-token prediction training promotes induction formation in small models, depending on size and data.

fits_no_version.finding: MTP-trained models outperform next-token models on polynomial arithmetic in and out of domain. The gain exceeds that from tripling model size.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Multi-token training improves synthetic algorithmic reasoning; not evidence of internal look-ahead in next-token models.

fits_no_version.finding: Extra heads of a 4-token model are accurate enough for self-speculative decoding: about 2.5 of 3 drafted tokens accepted on code, 3.0x speedup (Section 3.2, Table S2).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Trunk states of MTP-trained models support accurate several-token-ahead prediction; induced by training, so not V2 as stated.

record.problems: The induction experiments use a synthetic evaluation and report two independent runs; the authors note that the benchmark cannot reach a perfect score because some name tokens do not occur in training. They also use an epoch oracle based on the test metric. Key induction and arithmetic results are presented in figures without exact values in the text.
record.rows_left_out: No additional results bearing on the claim versions were identified. Broader code-generation, summarization, and inference-speed results evaluate the proposed training method but do not measure internal future-token representation or its causal effect on intervening text.

untested.parts: No rhyming verse, no frontier-model analysis, no intervention on planned words.
No readout of future tokens from a next-token model's hidden state. Future-token heads are trained jointly with the trunk. Pal et al.'s probing result is only cited.
Pre-caching is argued theoretically for MTP-trained models (Appendix L.2), not measured in next-token models.
No rhyme planning, attribution graphs or probing in open models.
Arithmetic and induction tasks measure accuracy after MTP training, not internal look-ahead. No chess or Sokoban.
No measure of plan depth or of whether plans steer generation.

record.verdict_notes: Planning-relevant material is discussion only: Appendix L.2 (precomputing features), L.3 (choice points, inconsistency-spotting circuits), L.4 (factorization orders), and a citation of Pal et al. (Future Lens, an original source). Self-speculative decoding results are absent from rows, but they concern the method's trained heads, not a version. Rows I1–A8 are correctly unlinked to versions.

versions.untested_parts: No rhyming-verse task, candidate rhyme-word representation measurement, or intervention changing a rhyme ending.
The study trains output heads to predict multiple future tokens but does not report a measurement of how accurately a single hidden state predicts tokens several positions ahead.

The study does not test whether next-token-trained models compute features for later positions independently of next-token prediction; its multi-token objective explicitly trains for future-token prediction.
No rhyme-planning test in smaller open-weight models and no open attribution-graph or probing-tool test.
The study evaluates induction and a synthetic arithmetic task after multi-token training, but does not measure internal look-ahead in those tasks or test chess or Sokoban.
No direct test of the depth of internal plans or whether a measured plan is merely a local next-token feature or heuristic.

relation.reason: Sections 5 and Appendix L discuss look-ahead and precomputation as explanations, without establishing the catalog's planning mechanisms or using an established finding as a tool.

tranche.reason: The study explicitly trains future-token prediction and evaluates its downstream benefits; it does not measure planning arising otherwise. Appendix K leaves its computation-sharing hypothesis unresolved.

source_check.notes: The rows report the study's training method versus baselines and should remain non-version-bearing method results. Individual plotted accuracies are not stated numerically; the authors' conclusion paraphrase is accurate.
